newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: KLM says sees further cut in govt stake.
newsitem.headline: KLM says sees further cut in govt stake.

text.p: KLM Royal Dutch Airlines said on Tuesday it expected the Dutch government to further reduce its 25 percent stake in the airline.

"In consultation with the government, KLM (last fiscal year) succeeded in further reducing the stake of the Dutch state...and there's more to come," outgoing KLM president Pieter Bouw told the airline's annual general meeting of shareholders.
"In order to avoid any misunderstanding, when I say 'more' I mean the state will have less," Bouw added.
Bouw, who steps down today, gave no indication of timing.
KLM bought back 17.3 million ordinary shares from the Dutch government in December 1996, reducing the state's stake to 25 percent from 38 percent in a one-billion-guilder deal.
The shares were later withdrawn, reducing KLM's capital base and boosting earnings per share by some 20 percent.
